_about: The locked answers to every question a chat session would otherwise ask.
This file is the reason the title is the only input. Each value here is a
decision that used to cost a round trip: how long, how many chapters, how
the hook opens, what counts as enough substance, what must never appear.
Do not treat unverified values as facts about the channel. Run
calibrate.py over real published scripts and it rewrites the numbers from
measurement; until then the ones marked default_unverified are starting
points chosen to be roughly right, not derived from the channel.

_provenance.structure.chapter_gap_seconds: measured — 0.30 s gap around a chapter title
_provenance.hook.target_words: derived — 25 s of hook at 180 wpm
_provenance.rhythm.sentence_len_stdev_min: default_unverified — calibrate.py sets this from real scripts
_provenance.substance.facts_per_100_words_min: default_unverified — calibrate.py sets this from real scripts
_provenance.banned_phrases: curated — general AI-writing tells, not channel-derived

shape: Every chapter answers one question and ends by opening the next.
A chapter that merely stops is where viewers leave.
Order chapters so each one reframes the last, not so they merely follow
chronologically — chronology is a filing system, not a reason to watch.

rules: Open on the strangest verifiable fact, stated flatly. No set-up.
The first sentence carries a number, a date, or a name.
State the contradiction the video resolves, then stop explaining it.
Never promise what the video will cover. Show the thing instead.
Close on the consequence, not a summary. The viewer already watched it.
One line of CTA at most, and it follows the payoff, never precedes it.
Never end on a rhetorical question aimed at the comments.
Vary sentence length deliberately. A short sentence after a long one is
the whole rhythm of the read.
One idea per sentence. Subordinate clauses stack badly when spoken.
Write for the ear: read it aloud in your head and cut what trips.
Every claim is attributable to a source in the research pack.
Prefer the specific to the summarised: 'forty-one ships' beats 'a fleet'.
If a fact cannot be sourced it does not go in, however good it sounds.
Contested facts are stated as contested, with who disputes them.

voice.tense: past for events, present for mechanisms
rules: Plain declaratives. The interest comes from the facts, not the adjectives.
No hedging: 'may have possibly been' is a fact you have not checked.
No addressing the audience as 'you' except in the outro CTA.
Numbers spelled the way they are said, not written as digits, when the
digit form would be ambiguous aloud.

banned_phrases: at the end of the day

rules: Primary and contemporary sources outrank encyclopaedias, which outrank
listicles and content farms. Never cite a source you did not open.
Two independent sources for any number that appears in the hook.
Record what could NOT be verified — that list is what stops an
unsourced claim reaching the script by default.
Note the strongest counter-argument to the video's angle. If it holds,
the angle changes; that decision is cheaper here than in a draft.
